children.text: Network learns weights
children.source: How does this network learn the appropriate weights and biases just by looking at data?
children.explain: The network learns the correct weights and biases by observing data.
children.mechanism: 1. Input data is presented to the network. 2. The network processes the data using current weights. 3. The network adjusts weights and biases based on the observed data.
children.example: A network learning to classify handwritten digits adjusts its internal parameters after seeing many examples of digits.
children.exercise: Describe one type of data (e.g., images, text) a network could use to learn appropriate weights.

children.text: Squish weighted sum

children.explain: This function squishes the relevant weighted sum into the interval between zero and one. It is motivated by the biological analogy of neurons being either inactive or active.
children.mechanism: 1. Calculate the weighted sum of inputs. 2. Apply the squishing function to the sum. 3. The output falls strictly between 0 and 1.
